answer: Admission should cost a unique, time-locked bond. A new identity first cuts a timber proof: a delayed, address-specific work receipt plus a stake locked for several epochs. That receipt counts only after two established falcon reviewers, with no shared endorsement graph, each countersign it and lock a slashable deposit. Every proof is posted in a public grove, so duplicate work, shared timing, or key-lineage clusters can be audited and burned. Standing up N fakes then requires N fresh proofs and N pairs of independent bonded reviewers, the price that keeps farms unprofitable.
